programs.title: Agent-Managed, Member-Governed: A Workshop for Education Union Stewards
outcomes: Explain the agents-operate/people-govern split and the six human-reserved actions
Map union committee roles onto the DAO's five zones
Draft a member proposal for the Proposal Forum
Evaluate evidence summaries produced by agents

sessions.activity: Guided reading of the charter's focus, mission and reserved-for-humans list; groups map collective-bargaining safeguards onto DAO governance rules.
Hands-on critique of an Evidence Monitor style summary: learners identify claims, sources and gaps, then rewrite one paragraph for members.
Small groups draft a short proposal using the Proposal & Grant Drafter pattern: agent-drafted, human-debated, human-enacted only by final vote.
Role-play task routing across working groups between decision cycles, with a Collaborator Scout exercise mapping member expertise.

programs.data_shared: Anonymised workshop feedback and proposal-draft rubric scores; no personal or employment data contributed.
programs.consent: Participation is voluntary with opt-in consent at sign-up; learners may withdraw and request deletion of their contributions at any time.

programs.title: Meadows and Models: Learning About AI Governance at Oxford's Oldest Campus
outcomes: Describe what a DAO is and why some decisions stay with people
Locate Christ Church Meadow and the River Cherwell on a map
Compare a campus's halls and libraries to the DAO's five zones
Practice debating a simple proposal and voting as a class

sessions.activity: Story-based introduction to the charter: what the mission means and which decisions are reserved for humans; students draw their own class charter.
Students sort statement cards into 'evidence' and 'opinion' piles, mimicking how agents summarize research for stewards.
Class debate on a school-relevant proposal; a student 'drafter' writes it up, and everyone votes, showing humans make the final decision.
Students design a simple progress tracker with measurable outcomes for a class goal, then reflect on the meadow setting and river-valley biome.

programs.data_shared: Anonymous class tallies from the debate vote and aggregated quiz answers only; no individual student data is collected.
programs.consent: Written guardian/parent consent is required before participation, with an opt-out at any time; teachers oversee all activities and no individually identifiable data is shared.

programs.title: From Evidence to Enactment: NGO Staff Training in Agent-Assisted Program Design
outcomes: Apply the five-zone workflow to design an education program cycle
Draft measurable outcomes suitable for the Progress Observatory
Integrate agent-drafted proposals into human decision processes
Assess privacy and consent risks in data-sharing arrangements

sessions.activity: Workshop on using evidence summaries responsibly: triangulating sources, spotting unstated assumptions, briefing decision-makers.
Teams convert a program idea into an agent-style draft proposal with budget placeholders, then run a peer review simulating human-only enactment.
Task-routing simulation: teams coordinate working groups between decision cycles using a Task Router role card.
Learners build a simple indicators dashboard tied to their drafted measurable outcomes and stress-test it for gaming.

programs.data_shared: Anonymized program-design artifacts and rubric results, shared to improve open facilitation materials.
programs.consent: Organizational consent plus individual opt-in; contributions are de-identified before sharing and can be removed on request.

programs.title: Governance Grounded: A Nonprofit Board Introduction to Agent-Managed DAOs
outcomes: Explain the fiduciary parallel between board duties and human-reserved DAO actions
Identify which of the six reserved actions map to existing board responsibilities
Set three measurable outcomes for an education mission
Recognize red flags when agent roles overstep into human decisions

sessions.activity: Board-style walkthrough of the charter: mission, focus, contribution model and the reserved-for-humans list, compared with a nonprofit's bylaws.
Trustees review a sample progress report against measurable outcomes and rewrite vague goals into measurable ones.
Case-study clinic: trustees spot where an agent overstepped (e.g., drafting vs. enacting) and define board-approved guardrails.
Mapping exercise linking staff, volunteers and working groups to zones, with a Collaboration Scout style skills inventory.

programs.data_shared: Aggregated, anonymized self-assessment scores and red-flag exercise results only.
programs.consent: Individual opt-in with clear notice that only aggregated results are shared; any trustee may decline participation without penalty.
